body:
Stephanie Nguyen: Debrief from the Northstar follow-up call (post-demo). They were generally positive, but we got a bunch of Qs we didn’t answer cleanly in the moment:
1) Dedicated SLAs (uptime + latency) + what’s actually “standard” vs negotiated
2) Private deployment: what exactly runs in their VPC, what we operate, and what audit/data retention story is for Private

Key quote: “If we move to Dedicated, what are you contractually committing to, and what happens when you miss it?”

Can we capture answers + update deck v1 with a cleaner slide/appendix? 

Markus Klein: +1. I was a bit hand-wavy on SLAs because we didn’t want to throw numbers on a live call. They asked:
- Dedicated uptime SLA (monthly?)
- Any latency SLA or just “targets”? (p95/p99?)
- Are credits automatic? does it require a ticket?
- Support coverage / response time when Dedicated is degraded

Also: Private: “Is it single-tenant control plane or shared?” and “Do prompts ever leave our network?”

Soojin Lee: Yep, we need to tighten the deck language. Right now slide 14 says “SLA-backed latency targets” but doesn’t define what that means. I can add an appendix slide that states safe wording + directs to security/commercial follow-up.

Question: what’s the approved phrasing? (No hard numbers.)

Naomi Feldman: For security angle, they asked me specifically:
- Where logs live in Private (our control plane vs their VPC)
- Whether audit logs can go to their SIEM
- Data retention defaults + ability to set to 0 / short retention

We should keep deck high-level but include: “Customer-controlled data plane in VPC, optional customer-managed logging destinations, encryption in transit/at rest, KMS integration.”

Lukas Meyer: From EMEA perspective, same questions always come up: “SLA in region” + “data residency.” If we add slides, please include a line that Private can be pinned to region and that Dedicated capacity is region-specific.

Markus Klein: I’ll paste the exact Qs from notes:
- “Is Dedicated actually single-tenant GPUs or just priority in a shared pool?”
- “If you have an outage on Hosted, do our Dedicated endpoints go down too?”
- “Private: do we run the runtime ourselves or do you manage it?”
- “Can you do on-prem or only VPC?”

I answered:
- Dedicated = reserved isolated capacity (single tenant pool)
- Dedicated is isolated from Hosted control-plane incidents “as much as possible” (not a great phrase)
- Private = customer VPC data plane + Redwood control plane components depending on option

We need a clean, consistent answer.

Simran Kaur: For the Dedicated isolation Q: we should be precise:
- Dedicated has dedicated GPU pool + separate routing policy/quotas.
- Control plane is still Redwood-managed, but Dedicated endpoints don’t contend with Hosted GPU capacity.
- If there is a control plane incident, Dedicated could be impacted depending on failure mode (auth/routing/etc). We can say “separate capacity plane; shared control plane with higher priority support + rollback paths.”

We should align with what we’re comfortable claiming.

Renee Sullivan: For talk track, we can add a standard “SLA answer block”:
- “We typically contract on uptime and have SLO targets for latency; exact terms depend on region + model + commit.”
- “Credits are part of the agreement; we can share sample language under NDA during procurement.”
- “Support: named channel + response-time commitments on enterprise tiers.”

Also: add a “Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private” table that says what’s shared vs isolated.

Soojin Lee: Action proposal for deck updates (v1.1):
A) Update wording on the Dedicated slide to avoid implying p95 latency is always contractually guaranteed.
B) Add appendix slide: “Dedicated SLA & Support (what we can state in a demo)” w/ bullets only.
C) Add appendix slide: “Private deployment boundary” (simple diagram + 5 bullets: data plane, control plane, logs, keys, updates).

Need inputs from Naomi + Markus on the bullet content.

Naomi Feldman: For the Private boundary slide, safe bullets:
- “Inference traffic stays within customer-managed network boundary (VPC) for Private deployments.”
- “Customer can integrate KMS/HSM for key management (deployment dependent).”
- “Audit logs available; export/integration to SIEM supported (Splunk/Datadog/etc) via standard sinks.”
- “Retention configurable; demo tenant defaults are short + sanitized (and not representative of customer policy).”

Avoid: “SOC2” claims on slides unless we have the approved wording. (We can say “security/compliance program available upon request.”)

Markus Klein: On Dedicated SLA slide, I’d like a line that answers the “what happens if you miss it?” question without numbers.
Maybe: “SLA credits as defined in MSA; incident communication + RCA provided for Sev-1/Sev-2.”

Stephanie Nguyen: +1. Also add a clear “don’t say this” note for AEs:
- Don’t promise p99 latency SLA unless it’s in writing.
- Don’t say “fully isolated from control plane incidents.”

Soojin Lee: Noted. I’ll add speaker notes in the deck + a callout in the talk track doc.

Simran Kaur: Minor but helpful: they asked “Can Dedicated burst?” We should answer consistently: yes, with pre-arranged burst capacity or autoscaling policy depending on contract/region. (Again, no numbers.)

Lukas Meyer: And for Private: always asked “how are upgrades handled?” We should mention pinned versions + controlled rollouts + canary.

Naomi Feldman: + “change management” is big for regulated folks. “Customer chooses maintenance windows / approval gates” (depending on package). Even if we keep it high-level.

Markus Klein: Who owns edits + by when? I have another Dedicated-heavy demo Thursday.

Soojin Lee: I can turn a draft by EOD tomorrow.
- I’ll update deck slides + speaker notes.
- Naomi: can you sanity check Private boundary bullets?
- Markus: can you review Dedicated SLA/support wording for field usability?

Stephanie Nguyen: Works. Please also post the final “approved phrases” in #sales so we stop freestyle answering SLAs.

Renee Sullivan: I’ll take a pass on the talk track once Soojin’s deck updates are in. Also adding a sidebar: “If they ask for SLA numbers → offer to follow up w/ standard language + connect procurement/security.”

Markus Klein: :thumbsup: I’ll drop the call notes excerpt here for completeness:
“Need Dedicated for predictable throughput, but leadership will ask what you guarantee. Private is likely required if we can’t keep prompts + logs inside our boundary. Also want to know who gets paged / response times.”

Naomi Feldman: :eyes: I’ll review. Also we should link the Security FAQ in the follow-up email template.

Soojin Lee: Draft plan:
- Deck v1.1: add 2 appendix slides (SLA/support + Private boundary)
- Speaker notes: add explicit safe talk track for SLAs + private components
- Optional: 1-line footnote on Dedicated slide: “Commercial terms vary by region/model/commit; see appendix.”

Stephanie Nguyen: Great. Tag me when draft is ready. 

(Reaction summary: Stephanie Nguyen added :thumbsup: to Soojin Lee’s draft plan; Markus Klein added :white_check_mark: to Naomi Feldman’s Private bullets.)
